intro: How long, since when and how long ago. Spanish uses the present for what is still true.
p.desde.consejo: It goes with a starting point: «desde 2020», «desde las nueve», «desde ayer». If there is a duration, use «desde hace».
p.desde hace.consejo: It goes with a duration and a present-tense verb: «vivo aquí desde hace dos años». It is like «for» in English.
p.hace.consejo: With a finished event it means «ago»: «llegué hace un mes». The h is silent and the c sounds «th».
p.cuánto tiempo.consejo: It asks about duration: «¿cuánto tiempo llevas aquí?». «Cuánto» has an accent because it is a question.
p.llevo.consejo: Here it does not mean «carry»: «llevo dos años aquí» counts the time up to now. The ll sounds like y.
p.llevas.consejo: For asking: «¿Cuánto tiempo llevas aquí?». It ends in -s, like all tú forms.
p.hasta.consejo: It marks the end: «trabajo hasta las dos». The initial h is silent: AS-ta.
p.durante.consejo: It measures how long something lasts: «viví allí durante tres años». With the indefinido, that period is over.
p.un mes.consejo: «Mes» is masculine: «un mes», «el mes pasado». It is pronounced with a single syllable: mes.
p.desde entonces.consejo: It picks up an earlier moment and continues to today: «empecé en enero; desde entonces estudio cada día».
p.empecé.consejo: Before e, z is written c: «empezar» becomes «empecé». The accent marks the last syllable.
p.llegué.consejo: Before e, the g needs a u to keep its hard sound: «llegar» becomes «llegué».
p.estudiando.consejo: It is used with «llevar»: «llevo un año estudiando español». -ar verbs form the gerund with -ando.
b1.texto:
If something began in the past and **continues now**, Spanish uses the **present**:

- Vivo aquí **desde** 2020. (starting point)
- Vivo aquí **desde hace** dos años. (period)
- **Hace** dos años **que** vivo aquí.
- **Llevo** dos años **viviendo** aquí. / **Llevo** dos años aquí.

Ask: **¿Cuánto tiempo llevas** aquí? **¿Desde cuándo** vives aquí?

If the event **has finished**, **hace** means «ago»: **Llegué hace dos años.**

**Durante** measures a duration: **Viví allí durante tres años.** The indefinido tells that time as closed.

From one point to another: **desde** las nueve **hasta** las dos, or **de** las nueve **a** las dos.
b2.titulo: How long have you been here?
b2.f0.texto: How long have you been in Madrid?
b2.f1.texto: I have lived here for two years.
b2.f3.texto: And have you been studying Spanish since then?
b2.f4.texto: I have been studying Spanish for a month.
b2.f7.texto: I work from nine until two.
b4.texto:
Each word does one job:

- **desde** + starting point: **desde** 2020, **desde** ayer, **desde** las nueve.
- **desde hace** + duration: **desde hace** dos años. The verb goes in the **present**.
- **hace** + duration + past verb: **llegué hace** un mes («ago»).
- **llevar** + duration (+ gerund): **llevo** dos años **estudiando**.
- **durante** + duration: **viví** allí **durante** tres años. The period is over.
- **hasta** marks the end: **hasta** las dos.

Ask with **¿Cuánto tiempo llevas…?** or **¿Desde cuándo…?**.

English says «I have lived here for two years»; Spanish says **vivo** aquí **desde hace** dos años.
b4.e0.texto: We have worked together for three years.
b4.e1.texto: I was in Lima for three weeks.
b4.e2.texto: We have been waiting for the train for two hours.
b5.f0.texto: I have lived by the sea for two years.
b5.f1.texto: Every morning, the wind brings a strong smell of salt.
b5.f2.texto: I have been walking along the beach every afternoon since autumn.
b5.f3.texto: Since then, the seagulls wake me with their sharp cries.
b5.f4.texto: I still do not know the name of all the streets.
b5.f5.texto: I arrived in this city a year ago with a single suitcase.
b5.f6.texto: During the first months, I walked aimlessly through unknown streets.
b5.f7.texto: I started working in a small bakery when winter came.
b5.f8.texto: Now I know all the neighbours on my street.
b5.f9.texto: My new life has smelled of warm bread for months.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Desde hace» needs a duration: «desde hace dos meses».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Hace» is used to say «ago» with a finished event.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Well done! March is a starting point: «desde marzo».
b6.pregunta: Which word marks a starting point?
b7.o0.refuerzo: It says you lived here and it is over.
b7.o1: Vivo aquí desde hace un año
b7.o1.refuerzo: Correct: it began a year ago and continues now.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Hasta» marks an end, not the time you have spent.
b7.pregunta: Which sentence means the same as «Llevo un año aquí»?
b8.traduccion: I have been studying Spanish for three years
b9.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «Hace» + time counts back from today.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Desde» needs a starting point, not a duration with a finished event.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Durante» measures how long something lasted, not how much time has passed since.
b10.o0.refuerzo: It asks for the time of day, not the duration.
b10.o1.refuerzo: It asks about the end of your stay.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «llevar» counts the time from the beginning until today.
b10.pregunta: Which question looks for the time up to now?
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Desde» marks the start of something that continues; here it is over.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Hasta» marks an end, not how long it lasted.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Well done! «Durante tres años» measures a closed period.
b12.pregunta: Which word measures the duration of something finished?
p.empezaste.consejo: The z in «empezar» sounds like th in Spain.
p.trabajamos.consejo: The j sounds like h: tra-ba-HA-mos.
p.caminando.consejo: The gerund ends in -ando in -ar verbs.
p.agudos.consejo: Adjective that agrees with «gritos», so it is plural.
